rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods <U+2013> two-year split-plot field experiment (2018, 2019) at Ludhiana comparing subsurface drip, surface drip and flood irrigation with four weed-control sub-plot treatments. Q2: Tables 1<U+2013>4 and Results <U+2013> in 2018 total weed density at 30 DAS was lower under SSD than SD and flood; at 60 DAS flood had higher total weed density and weed dry biomass than SD and SSD, with SSD lowest; in 2019 irrigation methods did not differ. Q7: Results and Discussion <U+2013> authors state that in 2019 no differential irrigation was applied because rain was sufficient and well distributed, hence irrigation methods showed no effect on weed density and biomass; the drip effect on weeds appeared only in the drier 2018 season when differential irrigations were applied.
rows.notes: The study supports only the weed-growth part of the claim; pests and fungus incidence were not assessed (the only pest/disease mentions are a deltamethrin spray and bacterial stalk rot removal applied uniformly). The stated mechanism in the passage (dry canopy) is not what the study tests; authors attribute lower weeds to drier upper soil under SSD, but this is asserted, not measured per treatment (TDR soil water was used only for the water balance), so Q4 is no. Weed density and biomass are both quadrat sampling, one method (Q3 no). Single site, single crop, plot scale (Q5, Q6 no). No explicit limitations stated (Q8 no). Only Tukey letter groupings, no SD/SE/CI (Q9 no).

notes: Full text appears complete. Table 5 text is garbled by column layout but the key weed and yield results are legible in Tables 1<U+2013>4, 6 and 7 and in the narrative.
